limits: All five original runs are retained: three pass and two fail the full 150 ms gate at 184 ms. Two subsequent CPU-profiled diagnostic repeats pass; they do not replace the failures.
The original module and studio maxima are 88 and 80 ms. The formerly blocked footnote interior phase is 64 ms, then 16 ms in its diagnostic repeat, versus 816 ms on 12.6.1.

Both 184 ms observations are primarily pre-handler queue delay. Neither overlaps an instrumented native call. The footnote delay overlaps an unattributed 168 ms Long Task; the late-body delay has no overlapping Long Task entry. The cause remains unproven.
CPU-profiled repeats were collected with other tool work paused; the spikes did not reproduce. An after-run snapshot of other host CPU activity cannot establish causation.
Native calls and background work can exceed 150 ms even when they do not overlap a sampled input. A passing input gate is not a bound on every task.
Serial production runs on one machine, not population INP or an editor-wide maximum. No application code changed between these seven runs.
Chrome Event Timing is quantized and collected with a 16 ms threshold. Key-to-rAF starts in the handler and excludes prior queuing.
All nine historical extended phases are retained at each target. Late-body and footnote targets match the previous 12.6.1 campaign.
Full structural layout after Enter is background work and may take seconds. Cold opening, exports, excluded native structures, compound edits and slower devices are not covered by a 150 ms claim.
